newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELA BOLIVAR ENDS LITTLE CHANGED IN SLOW MKT.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA BOLIVAR ENDS LITTLE CHANGED IN SLOW MKT.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed broadly flat at 494.00/494.75 per dollar Monday as moderate currency demand was covered by the Central Bank, traders said.
The bolivar closed at 494.00/495.00 per dollar Tuesday.
Traders said a small drop in interest rates following the Central Bank's weekly auction of monetary stabilization, or TEM, bills, did little to fuel currency demand.
Yields for six-month TEM bills, the benchmark for wider interest rates, fell 78 basis points to 21.89 percent at Wednesday's auction.
"The Central Bank was very active in the market," said one trader. "That and the reduction in demand for currency is encouraging exchange rate stability," he added.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
